subject.title: [AI] fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name in…

question: Should OpenClaw accept normalizing empty memory embedding `provider.model` values to the resolved adapter model at provider creation for existing upgraded indexes?
rationale: The code path is the right narrow source fix, but it changes the persisted/query identity seen by memory storage for users whose adapter previously returned an empty model, which is an upgrade-sensitive memory state decision under the repo policy.

options.title: Accept and land
options.body: Treat empty `provider.model` as a broken runtime state and land the centralized backfill with the included regression coverage.

options.title: Require migration proof first
options.body: Hold the PR until a maintainer asks for an explicit before/after upgrade test over an existing SQLite index with empty-model metadata.

options.title: Reject this normalization
options.body: Keep current provider objects unchanged and pursue a different memory repair strategy in the downstream identity/query layers.

recommendation.title: Accept and land
recommendation.body: Treat empty `provider.model` as a broken runtime state and land the centralized backfill with the included regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to this person as the strongest owner for the provider adapter boundary being changed.
